Theme

Playground equipment, sandbox toys, vehicles and play

gymnastics noun

also gymnast, do gymnastics, vaulting horse, pommel horse, horse (gymnastics), parallel bars, gymnastic

modern

Traupman 48

gymnastica, gymnasticae f.

noun, first declension

From the classical adjective gymnasticus (Plaut. Rud. 2.1.7: exercitū gymnasticō et palaestricō); Cicero says gymnicus.

Other words

  • ars gymnastica

    also used · modern · Traupman 64

  • exercitātrīx, exercitātrīcis f. — the art of training the body

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Quint. 2.15.25 (Lewis & Short)

    Quintilian’s Latin for Plato’s γυμναστική, bodily training in general rather than the modern sport.

  • gymnasticus, gymnastica, gymnasticum — gymnastic

    also used · classical · Plaut. Rud. 2.1.7: prō exercitū gymnasticō et palaestricō (Lewis & Short); Traupman 324

    Plautine; Cicero uses gymnicus (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • equuleus

    the vaulting horseTraupman 48

  • hastae parallēlae

    the parallel barsTraupman 356

See also gym, balance beam, sport, exercise, acrobat.
